messages:
Priya (Finance): Quick heads-up for the team — starting 2026-05-01 were updating several billing and quota behaviors that affect burst usage, free credits, and invoice timing. Please read; sharing with customers will be coordinated next week. :megaphone:

Tom (Ops): Thanks — high level what changes for latency-sensitive customers using burst pools?

Priya (Finance): Short answer: less surprise overages. Were introducing a 24-hour "burst-exemption window" for sudden short-term spikes, and a separate sustained-usage surcharge that only applies after a 7-day sustained threshold. That means brief spikes (under 24h) are exempt from burst overage billing once per 7-day rolling period.

Jules (Product): So we still charge if they keep spiking nightly? How do we define "sustained" exactly?

Priya (Finance): Good q. Definition (summary):
- sustained usage = > 50% of reserved throughput consumed for 7 consecutive days OR > 2x baseline for 7 consecutive days
- burst exemption = one contiguous spike period up to 24 hours per 7-day rolling window per account

Marta (Support): How will this appear on invoices / dashboard? Customers will ask.

Priya (Finance): Invoice & billing UX: were moving to an itemized batching window on invoices: invoices will be finalized on the 3rd business day of the month (instead of EOM immediate), with one line item called "Burst exemption credit" when the allowance applied. Well also add a short reason code. Example invoice snippet:```
{
  "invoice_date": "2026-05-03",
  "line_items": [
    {"code":"BASE_USAGE","amount":"$1,200"},
    {"code":"BURST_EXEMPTION_CREDIT","amount":"-$45","note":"1x 24h exemption applied"},
    {"code":"SUSTAINED_SURCHARGE","amount":"$200","note":"7-day sustained threshold exceeded"}
  ]
}
```

Finance Bot: Reminder: free credits deprecation timeline — free credits will begin phase-out for accounts that cross sustained-usage thresholds starting 2026-06-01. Accounts partially above the threshold will receive prorated credit adjustments and a 30-day notice.

Tom (Ops): Any immediate rate-limit changes? Will SDKs need updates to retry logic?

Priya (Finance): No rate-limit algorithm change. We are adding a soft-cap notification earlier (at 70% of quota) and one-time in-console guidance on batching/kv-caching to avoid hitting sustained thresholds. SDK retry semantics remain the same; the recommendation doc will be updated.

Jules (Product): Rollout plan? Customer comms?

Priya (Finance): Rollout plan: internal docs + help center published 2026-04-10; early-warning emails to affected customers 2026-04-20; public blog + billing FAQ 2026-04-30; enforcement begins 2026-05-01 for burst window and 2026-06-01 for free-credit phasing. Support and AE scripts will be shared tomorrow.

Marta (Support): Please drop the AE & support playbook link here when ready. Also want canned message templates.

Priya (Finance): Will do — sharing playbook + sample emails in #product-ops and #support-channels by EOD tomorrow.

Tom (Ops): Noted. We'll add dashboard soft-cap banners and a /quota-check endpoint for internal testing this week.

Jules (Product): Are there any exceptions (partners, trials)?

Priya (Finance): Exceptions: enterprise partners with negotiated terms and active trial accounts flagged as "pilot" are exempted until their trial ends. Well maintain a small "partner exemption" policy table.

Marta (Support): Thanks. One more: will refunds/credits be automatic or manual?

Priya (Finance): Credits for burst exemptions are automatic and appear as separate negative line items. Any disputed sustained-surcharge cases are routed to billing ops for manual review within 5 business days.

Finance Bot: Billing ops queue updated: #billing-appeals (rule id: BQ-2026-04).

Priya (Finance): If you have product or docs questions, ping me directly. Please hold off on external comms until we post the FAQ tomorrow. :handshake:
